main_text.head: Cap. 6. De articulo præposito vel omisso.
main_text.p: Articuli syntaxis præcipuè notabilis est, ut pro sua varietate modó præponatur, modó omittatur.
1. Præponitur articulato, nulla intercedente voce: ὁ εἶδος τῆς νόσου, species morbi: ὁ ἀκριβὲς τῆς ἐξετάσεως, accuratum inquisitionis, id est accuratio inquisitionis.
Aliquando tamen multi eleganter suis articulatis præponuntur: Æsop. ἡ τῶν θεῶν ὀργὰς ἀποσέπειν ἐπαγγελλομένην, deorum iras avertere pollicita.

2. Præponitur nomini cuilibet & proprio & appellativo. Demosthenes, ὑπω δὲ ἰῶ ὁ Φίλιππος ἐν φόβῳ, sic autem erat Philippus in metu. Polybius, οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι τὸ πρῶτον ἐπέθηκαν, Romani primùm invaserunt. Demosth. τὰς δεινὰς
ὁ ἀκριβὲς: the accent and breathing as printed; the last Greek phrase ends at the page foot.

page.notes: Greek text is transcribed as far as legible; some accents and final words near "δεινὰς" are uncertain and may be partly illegible in the scan. The catchword "deorum" is not clearly printed at the foot and may be a line end; treat with caution.
